title: Plum Box app manifest (manifest.json)
description: The rules plum-box-core (internal/apps/manifest.go) applies at install time. @plumbox/dev mirrors them in packages/cli/src/manifest.ts (a test keeps the two in step); the store's upload checks use this file directly.

id.description: Reverse-domain style, owned by the publisher's namespace (e.g. dev.alice.notes). Never changes for the life of the app.

entry.description: Bundle-relative HTML the panel opens with.

mobile.description: Shown in the phone apps' launchpad.

mimeTypes.description: Types this app can open from Drive.

bin.description: Bundle-relative arm64 Linux ELF, started once per user under the app's own uid.

cpu.description: Percent of one core; 100 = one core. Default 50, cap 200.

clients.description: Companion apps (native clients) that may obtain delegated access under this app's id through OAuth. The store registers them on upload; a box also honours them straight from an installed manifest (a paired developer can test a companion app without the store).

display_name.description: What the box's consent screen shows.

redirect_uris.description: Native targets only: a custom scheme (myapp://cb) or http loopback (127.0.0.1 / ::1 / localhost, any port). Never https.

scopes_allowed.description: Subset of files:read, files:write, user:profile, service:call:<manifest.id>. read/write are aliases.

protocols.description: Standard-protocol mounts the app's service answers. Core proxies these paths to the service verbatim — the request path, Destination header and body hrefs all arrive unchanged — and adds X-Plum-Mount. Requires server and the service:call permission. Authentication is a PAT scoped service:call:<manifest.id>, over Bearer or as a Basic password; a session cookie is never accepted on a mount.

mount.description: Exactly "/dav/<manifest.id>/", or that plus ONE more [a-z0-9._-] segment (e.g. /dav/dev.alice.cal/calendars/). JSON Schema cannot compare one property against another, so this pattern only checks the shape; that the id in the path is THIS manifest's id — which is what makes squatting another app's mount, or the box's own /dav/files/, impossible — is enforced by plum-box-core (apps.validateProtocols) and by the store (app/checks.py). Two entries may not share a mount.

then.description: A mount with no service behind it is a 503 generator, and service:call is the permission the owner sees and can switch off.
